reading:
Night Timetable (r10-wild-3, main round 10, #12 of 19, mean 6.55 against today's 4.29, in two top fours with 4 promise votes) was judged in one round only. The panel split between 8.1 (style) and 5.5 (soul), and the split tells the story.

WHAT THE JUDGES LOVE (every lens named some of it):
- Vera's conversation drawn as the line down the middle of a three-column Home: her screen, the question as the first stop, the ways to start as stops hung on spurs, "Continue with Vera" as the terminus. Feedback called it "the owner's favourite element". Style: "a genuine system ... the most joy of any entry". Interaction: "the most glanceable Home".
- The Chat as a printed timetable: bold tabular times in the margin, the date given once, and the line ending at a lit ring by the box ("your turn").
- The departure board. Soul: "glows brightly". Feedback: "raster-lit".
- Numbered enamel lines as a real wayfinding grammar (a number, a colour and a sign per place).
- Confident, big, warm type: Archivo in two widths and a written token scale.
- The Settings nav drawn as a line of stops (not remarked, but it is the idea carried through).

WHAT SANK IT was costume and colour load, not the idea. The faults, most-cited first:
1. Too many colours. Five pastel number discs in the bar, a rainbow rule under the bar, filled yellow arrow tiles, a hazard stripe, copper-brown family bubbles and a yellow cap and "here" tile on Status (feedback, soul, system, skeptic, style).
2. The hazard stripe on setup (five lenses), which is also drawn before the ask but reached after it by Tab (interaction, usability).
3. Number discs in place of the icons in the bar and on the phone tabs (interaction, usability, skeptic, soul).
4. The glass greeting pool is gone (feedback, soul, system).
5. 34 of 57 Home targets under 44px (interaction, usability).
6. The chat is one-sided: both speakers sit on the left (interaction, usability, skeptic, and lessons' open problem).
7. Heads too heavy (style, system, type), boxed title plates (style, system; they push the Plans week below the fold, usability), and side columns that wrap titles (type).
8. Doto fuzzy below board size. Soul and interaction want VT323; type wants Doto only at 20px and up.
9. A dead lower half in Home's middle column (style, system).
10. The open select loses its ring (usability).
11. To do shows no late and prints "27 Sep 2026, 19:56" beside OPEN chips. That is the lessons' open problem: late in amber words.

The soul lens's deficit is the light. The rail itself was the brightest green on the page (7.3 per mille) while the pool, the halos and the key word's bloom were weak (glow 0.7, screenGlow 0.9, topGlow 0.5). That is the reverse of "light is a list".

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WIN:
- Keep the line, the timetable Chat and the board exactly as ideas.
- Strip the costume: steel numerals and icons, enamel only on the current line and one sign rule, no tiles, no hazard, slate bubbles with copper only in the edge and initial, steel for "here".
- Put the phosphor back on the short list at full strength: the lit stop you are at, the pool under the ask, the board as a true tube with bloom and scanlines, the radar, her screen, lamps, Send, the key word.
- Restore mine-versus-hers in the chat without losing the time margin.
- Carry the timetable through To do (due times in the margin, late in amber words, a lit Now), Plans, Status and Settings.
- 0 small targets, lighter heads and unboxed nameboards.

The later rounds say structure plus meaning wins (lines that carry order, light that carries data). They also say the owner values fine line art that leads the eye through every page, which is this lineage's native tongue.

The tour has judged no greeting titles yet, so no title is carried. The carried page still asks "What's on your mind?", and each brief proposes a new one in the station's voice.

briefs.name: Timetable Relit
briefs.hypothesis: The judges liked this lineage's bones more than any other wild entrant's: her line down Home, the timetable chat and the departure board. It lost on the colour load and costume laid over them (five candy discs, a rainbow rule, yellow tiles, a hazard stripe, brown bubbles), on a one-sided chat and 34 small targets, and on the light going to the rail instead of the phosphor. Remove the costume and keep every structure. Put exact #6dff9c at full kit strength only on the short list: the stop you are at, the pool under the ask, the board, the radar, her screen, lamps, Send and the key word. Tell mine from hers while the times stay in the margin. Then carry the timetable to To do, Plans, Status, Settings and the form. The result should score like the style lens's 8.1 on every lens: a calm station at night where the only lights are live ones.
briefs.brief:
Start by copying /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t1-a/variants/r10-wild-3/ (sheet.css and templates _ui.html, base.html, chat.html, home.html, ideas.html, tasks.html) and palettes/r10-wild-3.json. Add copies of _ask.html, plans_month.html, status.html, settings.html, settings_section.html, new_idea (form), login.html and 404.html from /home/user/FamilyDB/src/familydb/web/templates/ where you change them. It stays a clean sheet.

0. TOKENS. Keep the lineage's warm-white-on-night, and move the plates off teal onto a steel slate that leans toward green-black:
- bg #0b0f0d; surface #131a1d; surface-2 #182125; surface-3 #1f292e; field #0c1214
- line #222b2f; line-2 #303b40; card-edge #2b363b; edge #6d7a80
- ink #dcd7cb (about 12.5:1); ink-2 #bcb7ac; dim #a29e94; faint #948f87; heading #ebe6da
- label #a9b3b8 (steel, replacing khaki #b7b19c); secondary #c4cdd2
- bubble #111712 (her glass); bubble-them #182125 (slate, not copper-brown #272017)
- bezel #232b2e; bar #0e1416
- brand, screen #6dff9c exact; brand-hover #92ffb8; lit #86d9a6
- accent #e6d595: the wayfinding yellow, lower in chroma, for links and their arrows only, never a fill
- people #d9a27c: copper, for the family's initials and names only
- ideas #b694d5, plans #99d4f3, todo #89d4cf, shows #e6a0ba, seasons #e88671 and outing #a8d88f as now; danger #f2716a
- In sheet.css define --late: #f0b04f (amber, one job: late and needs-a-look) and --steel: #9db3c2.
- Line 1, Vera, becomes the steel 'main line' (.in-chat{--line-c:var(--steel)}), so no rail anywhere is green.
- Set glow 1.0, screenGlow 1.0 and topGlow 1.0 in the JSON. In a clean sheet the light itself must be written as kit CSS (below).

1. BAR (base.html; the sheet's .bar and .places). Every place gets its Lucide icon back and its word: Home, Vera, Ideas, Plans, To do, Wishes.
- The line number becomes a small steel badge on the icon's top-right: a 1rem disc with a 1.5px #5b666f ring, the numeral in Archivo condensed 600 at .6875rem, tabular.
- Current place: a latched steel cell (background #1f292e, 1px #3a4850 edge, inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255/.06)). Its badge disc fills with that line's enamel (numeral in --on-bright), its icon takes the enamel, and a 3px bar in the enamel sits under the item, flush on the bar's bottom hairline. On Status, Settings, Memory and Family the same cell has a steel 3px bar. That is the one drawing of 'here'; delete the yellow Status tile and the yellow gear tile.
- The tools nav (Memory, Family, Status, Settings) shows icon plus word from 72rem up, icon only with aria-labels below that.
- Delete .bar::after's full-width line colour and Home's five-segment rainbow. The bar's lower edge becomes one 1px steel hairline, and the bar is drawn at 88% alpha so the E6 top haze breathes under it.
- Keep the footer's five short line segments as the only map key (the colophon).
- Every item gets min-height 2.75rem.
- Phone tab bar: icon over word, with the number badge on the icon. The current tab is the latched cell with its icon in the enamel and a 2px enamel cap on the top edge (steel on Home).

2. PAGE HEADS (_ui.html page_head). Drop the boxed title plate with its coloured top cap. The nameboard is unboxed:
- a 2.75rem line disc: a 2px enamel ring, the numeral in heading ink, Archivo condensed 600;
- h1 in Archivo 600 at wdth 110, clamp(2.1rem, 1.6rem + 1.6vw, 2.75rem), -0.02em, line-height 1.02;
- the lede at 1.0625rem ink-2, max 58ch;
- the page's one primary action (E3 green) on the title's baseline at the right;
- under the whole head, one 2px rule in the line's enamel over a 1px steel rule that runs to the edge (the sign's band).
- Facilities (Status, Settings, Memory, Family, the settings pages) get a 2.75rem square steel tile with the pictogram and a steel band.
- Head height is about 120px, so the Plans month's current week fits in 900px.
- Crumbs ('← Ideas', '← Settings') are sentence case, 44px, in the link yellow: no tracked caps.

3. HOME (home.html). Keep the three columns, with her line in the middle as the hero: grid-template-columns: minmax(20.5rem,1fr) minmax(30rem,1.2fr) minmax(20.5rem,1fr), gap 1.75rem, 1px steel column rules. Below 78rem her column spans the top and the other two sit side by side under it. Row titles get text-wrap: balance.

MIDDLE (her line):
- The rail is 3px steel #3a4a50, never green. It starts under her screen (E19 presence at 2.75rem, glyphs falling once) beside '① Vera' and the date as plain condensed-caps label text (.06em), with no boxed chip.
- Stop 1 is the ask. A 1.1rem hollow steel ring on the rail with a spur to the plate. On .welcome .ask:focus-within the ring lights as a kit lamp (E20): border and centre dot var(--brand), box-shadow 0 0 6px var(--brand), 0 0 18px color-mix(in srgb,var(--brand) 45%,transparent), in 0.12s and out over 1.2s.
- The ask plate sits in the restored glass pool (E7). The middle column's .welcome gets radial-gradient(70% 90% at 0% 100%, color-mix(in srgb,var(--brand) 13%,transparent), transparent 62%), plus the ::before scanlines (white 2.8%, 1px in 4) masked to that pool, so the light rises from where the line meets the box.
- The plate: background rgb(9 12 11/.72); border color-mix(in srgb,var(--brand) 30%,var(--line-2)); resting halo 0 0 38px -20px brand 60%; the E4 focus bloom; the textarea on field #0c1214.
- The title h1 (see the title field) keeps the E1 two-layer halo on its lit word at 45%/22%, not the carried 40%/18%.
- FROM, the mic and Send (E3 ring and 8px pool, the only filled green on the page) sit on one row, with 'Send where I am' under them.
- Stops 2-4 are the ways to start. 0.85rem steel rings on the rail, with 1.25rem spurs to buttons that are slate #182125 with a 1px #34424a edge, min-height 2.75rem, ink 500 at 1rem, and no yellow left edge. Hover: a 12% steel wash and a 2px lit inset edge, fading over 1.2s (E9).
- When talk.line exists, her last reply is a stop, her glyph screen on the rail.
- Terminus: a double ring (1.5rem steel outer, a steady 0.45rem phosphor centre with the two-layer halo). 'Continue with Vera →' in the link yellow, underlined, 1.0625rem 600, 44px. No arrow tile.
- Under the terminus, the setup notice moves here, after the ask in source and drawn after it (the Tab order now matches). It is a slate plate (surface) with a 2px --late rule on its top edge, no hazard stripe and no fill:
  - h2 '▲ Finish setting up' in sentence case, 600, 1.3125rem;
  - the 'Each one is a short page…' line;
  - the three steps as a short vertical line: a 2px steel rail with a hollow --late ring per step, each step's sentence an underlined link;
  - 'All the setup steps' at the foot.
  This also fills the dead lower half of the middle column.

LEFT:
- The Next up departure board: a thin graphite case, not a slab. padding .4rem .4rem 1rem, radius 14px, background linear-gradient(#20282b,#161c1f), 1px #2c3538, the E12 inset highlight and 80px spill, a chin of 2px vent slots and the E12 power light.
- The tube is VT323 at 1.5rem with the E13 halos and 0.35px blur, the E14 scanlines, sheen and falloff, and a faint 8% dot pitch (radial dots at 3px) as the board's matrix. Drop Doto everywhere.
- On the tube: a 7.5rem E17 radar top-right with blips and sweep; 'NEXT UP' in E15 inverse; the title at 2rem bright; the when line; '[TODAY]' bright in brackets; and '> 4 more on the radar' with the cursor, nowrap scoped to the link.
- Coming up (sign ③) becomes a printed timetable, the strip the owner liked. Each row:
  - a slate date leaf (#1a2327): 'Thu' above, the day at 1.5rem Archivo condensed 600 tabular, 'Oct' below in label ink;
  - the title as a link (600, 1.0625rem, underline on hover and focus only) with the location under it in ink-2;
  - a right facts column: the time (split entry.when after ', ') in condensed 600 tabular, over the relative ('in 2 days') in ink-2 sentence case. No caps pill.
  Rows are ruled by hairlines, with the E9 afterglow on hover. Today's row gets a steel latched leaf and a small phosphor lamp.
- The kids' wishes (sign ⑤) follow as rows.

RIGHT:
- To do (sign ④): each tick box is a 1.25rem box in a 44px hit area (negative margin). The title is 600 1.0625rem with no wrap at the new width. The meta shows the owner, then late as --late words ('was due 2 days ago'), and the late box gets a 1.5px --late edge.
- Lately added (sign ②): one-line rows. The kind is an icon plus the word in its kind colour, sentence case .875rem, with no filled tile and no caps; then the title 600; then 'for Maya, Theo'.
- 'Something to eat' is a slate row with a steel chevron.

SECTION HEADS everywhere: the steel number badge, h2 in Archivo 600 at 1.3125rem, and one 2px rule in the line's enamel under the head. The link at the right is sentence case and underlined ('All plans', 'All 4', 'Add an idea' with a plus icon), 44px via padding and negative margin. No ALL caps and no yellow tiles.

Phone order: her line, the notice, the board, Coming up, To do, Lately added, wishes. The question stays on one line: font-size clamp(1.9rem, 7.5vw, 2.5rem) at wdth 100.

4. CHAT (chat.html; _ui.html chat_line). Keep the timetable with the times in the margin and give each side its own place. Each li is a grid of 4.75rem (times), 2.75rem (the rail) and minmax(0,1fr).
- The day is given once as a dateline row, 'Sunday 27 September', in condensed caps .06em across the margin and the rail, where the day changes. Times are Archivo condensed 600 .9375rem, tabular, right-aligned.
- Her stops: her screen (E19) on the steel rail. Her bubble is justify-self start, max 62ch, on glass #111712 with a 1px color-mix(brand 22%) edge; 'Vera' in lit 600 .875rem.
- The family's stops: a 2rem disc on the rail with a copper 1.5px ring and the copper initial on slate. A 1px dotted steel spur (45%) runs from the stop to their bubble, which sits justify-self end, max 46ch, slate #182125 with a 1px #2e3a40 edge and an inset 3px copper edge on its right side, the name in copper.
- The newest stop is lit (brand ring, the E20 halo) and its time is in brand. On :target #latest the bubble flashes E10 and fades.
- The rail ends at a hollow ring beside the composer that lights while the composer has focus ('your turn'). The composer is glass with the E4 focus, FROM, the mic and Send on one row, and 'Send where I am' under them.
- The kids' conversations become a small 'branch line' panel with steel rings and 44px links.
- Phone: the rail at 1rem, the time moved into the said-by line at the right, and family bubbles indented 2.5rem with their copper edge.

5. IDEAS (ideas.html):
- Unboxed nameboard ②, with 'Add an idea' E3 on its baseline.
- 'Save a thought for later' as a slate fold with a 44px summary.
- All ideas | Restaurants as a segmented pair: the current one latched steel with a 3px lilac under-bar.
- Filters on one row (Search 1.6fr, Kind, Status, For, then a steel secondary Filter button). Labels in condensed caps .06em. appearance: base-select pickers with ::picker(select) on slate, a latched steel option and a lit tick; select:open,select:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--brand);outline-offset:2px}.
- From 64rem: the list (1fr) with a sticky portrait 'On the radar' board beside it (20rem, the same thin case): an 11rem radar on top, then '10 places from home' and the Nearest/Furthest lines with the distance nowrap, and the reading note under the case.
- The list is a destinations timetable of one-line rows: #id in condensed tabular label ink (3rem); the kind (icon plus word in its colour); the title (600 1.0625rem link); 'for …' in ink-2; and the drive time right-aligned in condensed tabular as the facts column.
- '12 ideas' is set as the list's sign head. Keep .idea-card on each row.

6. PLANS MONTH (plans_month.html; the carried rules):
- Nameboard ③.
- List | Month as the segmented pair.
- 'September 2026' in Archivo 600 at 2rem, with Earlier / Later as 44px secondaries on the same baseline.
- The grid is a printed timetable. Heads 'Mon … Sun' in condensed 600 .8125rem sentence case, tracking .04em (no tracked caps); transparent hairline cells on a slate tray; day numerals in condensed tabular 600; outside days faint.
- Today: a steel inset outline plus a 0.5rem phosphor lamp with the two-layer halo before its numeral. Not yellow, not amber.
- Plan chips in cells: slate #1f292e with a 2px left edge in the plan's kind colour, the time in condensed tabular, the title 500 .8125rem.

7. TO DO (tasks.html). The line's own timetable:
- Nameboard ④ with its lede.
- The 'Add something to do' fold as a slate plate with a 44px summary.
- Show becomes one segmented control (Open · Done · Cancelled · All as links to url_for('web.tasks', status=…) with the q kept, latched steel for the current one), plus the Search field and a secondary button. Remove the Show select, so there is one control per filter.
- Each row is a grid of 7.5rem (due margin), 2.75rem (rail), 2.75rem (tick) and minmax(0,1fr), with 'Edit' at the end.
  - The margin: right-aligned, nowrap, condensed 600 .875rem. Late reads 'was due 2 days ago' in --late. Upcoming reads 'in 2 days' over '19:56'. No date reads 'No date' in faint.
  - Compute late exactly as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t1-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/tasks.html does (the due_words macro, lines 28-36; clock_today = config.FAMILYDB_APP.clock.today(), lines 103-104; the late test, line 137).
  - The rail is a 2px todo-enamel line at 55%, with a stop per task: a filled --late ring when late, a hollow steel ring otherwise.
  - Between the last late row and the first upcoming row sits a Now rule: a 1px steel line across, a 0.55rem phosphor lamp with the two-layer halo on the rail, and 'Now' in condensed caps.
  - The meta: owner, reminder (bell) and the exact date 'Sun 27 Sep, 19:56' with no year.
  - Drop the OPEN chips while Open is shown.
  - 'Edit, complete, or snooze' becomes a 44px 'Edit' summary with the pencil at the row's end; its form opens across the row.

8. STATUS (status.html):
- Facility nameboard with a steel tile and no yellow cap.
- Who answers, Keys and Connected to as three slate trays (#11171a) with a 2px steel sign rule and no box-in-box.
- Each row puts its lamp in a left column. On is the E20 lit dot with an 8px and 18px halo, breathing 3.2s. Off is a 2px pewter ring (#8794a2), not red. Part is an amber half. Red is kept for stopped.
- 'What it has cost' is a spend board in the thin case, VT323.
- The 'Change a key' link is underlined.

9. SETTINGS:
- The overview's nine cards become flat slate plates (a 2px steel top edge, the pictogram tile in steel, the title 600, the status lines ink-2). The whole plate is the 44px link, with a plain steel chevron in place of the yellow arrow tile.
- 'Needs a look' is a --late ring badge in sentence case with ▲. The card's edge stays steel, with --late only on the badge and a 2px left edge.
- Section pages keep the nav as a line of stops. The current stop is a filled steel ring plus a latched row, not yellow.
- The sticky save bar keeps its E3 Save.

10. FORM (new idea):
- Nameboard ② with the '← Ideas' sentence-case crumb.
- Fields are filled, bounded boxes (#0c1214, 1px edge) with E4 focus, the caret in brand and the mic inside.
- Labels in condensed caps .06em.
- 'Add it' (E3) and 'Cancel' (steel secondary), both 44px.
- input[type=checkbox]:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--brand);outline-offset:2px}.

11. SIGN IN / 404:
- The same thin case, E16 power-on from opacity .05, the E22 face with blinking eyes, and 'READY.' with the E15 cursor. The plate's green cap becomes a 2px steel rule.
- The 404 board is a 4:3 tube with the radar, '404' flickering (E18) and the readout beside it.

12. TYPE SYSTEM, written into :root:
- Archivo only, plus VT323 on the glass. Heads 600, rows 500, body 400; strong 600.
- Seven steps: name clamp(2.1–2.75rem); question clamp(1.9–2.75rem); sign 1.3125; item 1.0625; body 1 (line-height 1.55); small .875; label .8125 condensed caps at .06em. Drop the .75 stamp step (the smallest is 13px).
- font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums in every time and figure column; text-wrap: balance on heads and titles; pretty on paragraphs; bubbles 62ch, ledes 58ch.
- Controls and see-more links are always sentence case.

13. LIGHT, as kit CSS written with color-mix(var(--brand)):
- E1 on the key word.
- E2 on the mark: bloom, the icon's drop-shadow at 75% and the caret blinking 8 times.
- E3 on Send and one primary per page, with other buttons as flat steel secondaries.
- E4 on every field, and Home's resting halo.
- E5 as one 2px focus ring offset 3px.
- E6 top haze: html radial 60% 38% at 50% -10%, brand at 7.5%.
- E7 as above; E8 as the 3.5% edge light on plates; E9 afterglow on rows and cards; E10 landing on #coming and #latest.
- E12-E17 on the boards and the radar; E19 her screen; E20 lamps; E21 the done tick and the chosen card.
- Copy the kit's Access blocks: reduced motion, more contrast (scanlines, halos and blur off) and forced colours.
- The rail and the enamel never glow. Measure the bright-green share: it should fall below the carried 7.3 per mille while the halos read at 100%.

14. TARGETS: 0 of 57 on Home under 44px (bar items, badges, see-more links, starters, ticks, add, the terminus link), with the same on To do, Ideas and Settings.
briefs.borrows:
From this lineage's own judges, most-cited first:
- Cut the colour load (feedback, soul, system, skeptic, style). Plain steel numerals with only the current line in enamel (feedback, soul). Enamel only on the disc and one rule under each sign (system). The rainbow bar rule dropped (soul, system), keeping the five segments only in the footer key (style's 'segmented rule').
- The hazard stripe becomes one amber rule (feedback, soul, style, system, skeptic).
- Yellow arrow tiles become plain underlined sentence-case links with plain arrows (feedback, style, skeptic), and 44px (interaction).
- Family bubbles on slate with a copper edge and initial instead of the brown fill (feedback, skeptic), set right against the margin timetable (interaction, usability).
- 'Here' in steel, one drawing everywhere, no yellow on Status (system, interaction, feedback).
- The glass greeting pool restored behind the ask stop (feedback, soul, system).
- Icons back in the bar and phone tabs with small number badges (skeptic, interaction, usability, soul).
- Heads one weight lighter (style, system, type).
- Boxed title plates dropped for an unboxed nameboard with its rule (style, system; usability's Plans fold).
- VT323 on the board with Doto dropped (soul, interaction), keeping the board's matrix as a faint dot pitch (feedback's 'raster-lit').
- The radar back on Home's Next up (style).
- The dead lower half filled with the setup notice under the terminus (style, system). The notice moved after the ask for Tab order (usability, interaction).
- Wider side columns and balanced titles (type).
- Condensed caps capped at .06em (type).
- The open select's ring (usability).
- 44px everywhere (interaction, usability).

From the tour's and the tournament's standing asks:
- Late in amber words on To do, with the recipe from r13-idea-1/templates/tasks.html (lessons' open problem).
- One control per filter on To do.
- The kit's light on the phosphor list only (phosphor_kit.md E1-E22).
- The Ideas list first with a portrait scope beside it (lessons round 6).
- Coming up as Galley Rack-shaped strips (date leaf, title, facts column), which the owner praised.

Nothing structural is imported from another lineage.
briefs.title:
What’s the *plan*? It is the family's own sentence, what one parent says to the other on a Friday evening, and it says FamilyDB's job in one word: a planner. It covers what the box takes (a weekend, an idea to keep, a reminder, something for the calendar) and invites telling Vera rather than confiding a mood. The lit word 'plan' is the product's job, and it also names the station's timetable, the thing her line is. At 16 characters it fits one line on a phone at the question size. Set it in _ask.html as

, with the curly apostrophe, still the textarea's label. The placeholder ('Plans for the weekend, an idea to keep, a reminder, the calendar…') then reads as its answer.

briefs.name: Night Departures
briefs.hypothesis:
The timetable idea is strongest where time is literally a line and the lit glass shows the family's own departures. Four features lost with weaker packages would each turn one of this lineage's pages into its purest form:
- Zenith Desk's meridian makes the Chat a two-sided timetable, the line itself the spine, Vera on one side, the family on the other and the times on the line. That ends the one-sided log three lenses faulted.
- Plotting Room's departures record makes Next up a real departure board listing the next four plans on lit phosphor leaders. The glass then carries data (the lessons' 'light as data') instead of one line on a slab, and it replaces a duplicate list.
- Single Quote's one-line setup strip makes the hazard-striped notice a quiet service notice hung under her terminus, so the ask leads the eye and the Tab order.
- Signal Box's two ends of a line make Sign in the platform you board at and the 404 the buffer stop at the end of the line.
With the lineage's key fixes applied, the station reads on every page, the light returns where it means something, and the costume that sank round 10 is gone.

briefs.title:
What’s *next* for us? A family's own question on a Sunday night. 'For us' makes it the household's voice, and 'next' covers everything the planner holds: the next outing, a plan for the calendar, a reminder, an idea to keep, a wish. The lit word 'next' is the station's word. It echoes the departure board's 'Next up' two columns away, so the question at her line's first stop and the board's first departure speak the same language. It invites telling Vera what comes next rather than asking how anyone feels. At 20 characters it fits one line on a phone at clamp(1.75rem, 7vw, 2.5rem) in Archivo at normal width. In _ask.html:

, still the textarea's label, with a curly apostrophe.
